speaker: Speaker 1
words: The following interview is of Linda Apple, May 20, 1975, at St. Mary's, Idaho, by Irma Wood.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Okay, now I'll watch it. Okay. What are some of the advantages and the disadvantages of living in St. Mary's?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, a lot of the advantages we have is our recreation, our hunting, our fishing. It's a small community, not a big city. And the disadvantages, of course, you don't have your shopping and stuff as you do in the big cities, which we go to Spokane a lot to do a lot of that, which I think most everybody here does.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: It isn't too far from Spokane, is it?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: No, it's what, approximately an hour and a half, if you're going slow like me, to get there. Spend the day and come home. It's not bad.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Now, it says, how does your family life compare with the family life when you were a child? Now, you didn't live in, did you live in St. Mary's?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: No, we lived in Redmond, Oregon when I was a child, and of course, the area there was different than St. Mary's. It was flat, sagebrush, and juniper trees, which I still like. Yeah. And we lived on a farm. And of course, here we live on a farm and we have cows and our steers and stuff, but not like then. It's always different when you're a child.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Yes. But you do have animals here.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yeah, they're not here at the moment, but they're up at his dad's for the summer while

speaker: Speaker 2
words: we've got it. Just cows. Do you have a horse?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: No, we did have, but we sold her because we didn't have our fences up after the flood or anything and it became an ocean. She was a pet, she was born here, and we just spoiled her rot and she got too big. You couldn't handle her. And Wendy has rabbits, and of course the dogs and the cats.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: You have four children?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Five. Five children. Four girls and one boy.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And what are their ages and interests?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Cheryl is 15 and her interests are sewing, cooking, and her band, active in school with her band activities. Ginger is 14 and she was active in youth club at the Presbyterian Church and the different things they did, and in pet band, and she loves the outdoors. Jackie, she's 12. And she's in band and she loves to be active in sports. They all seem to be active in sports. And Wendy, she's eight, nine. Nine. Nine. She's getting old. And she likes the outdoor activities. None of them are really indoor or like to go around inside too much. They like to get out and be active. Of course the baby, he's just whatever.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: He's two.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yeah, he'll be two. He loves it outside. He'd sleep out there if we let him.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: You have a beautiful, beautiful home here. I wonder if you could tell something about it.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, when we went through the flood in January, we moved our house back, what was it, about 700 feet or something back anyway by the river and put it on a foundation so that we could we wouldn't have to worry about the flood anymore. And it overlooks the river from all directions. We have a beautiful view of Baldy. And of course the lake out in the middle of the valley, it's beautiful at night when the moon shines on it and stuff. It's like a picture. And I don't know, it's just a beautiful valley, we think. We love it here.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I understood the flood went right through your house.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yes, we had approximately five and a half feet of water in our home. Lost quite a few things and a lot of things destroyed by flood that it didn't take with it. And it was quite a chore cleaning that up.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I noticed in your pictures the water went clear to the windows of your house.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yes, it was quite deep. It really soaked up the walls and everything. Went through it all. Childbearing.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: And your recreation, you've told a little bit about that, about the... things that you enjoy. You told about what you like.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: I enjoy fishing for recreation, just go behind the house. Or in the wintertime we have two snow cats and we can just go right out here in the field and snow cat and have a ball.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Oh, that sounds like fun.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Anytime a person has enough snow to do it. And it is fun. And kids enjoy it. We didn't have time this year to go on any snowmobile trips. Maybe next year. And our family does most everything together. Snow catting, fishing, picnicking. Going to a show or something, we usually do that together. Or go to the lake or whatever.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: What does your husband do for a living?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: My husband, he works for Potlatch as a contractor, logging. And he's been with them, I think this will be his third year with them. Before that him and his dad worked together and he was a sawyer before that.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Oh yeah, he's always been in logging.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yes, since we were married he's been in logging.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Was he raised in St. Mary's?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yes, he was born here in St. Mary's.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: That's how you became a St. Mary's citizen, I guess.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yeah, I guess so.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I know it says what community projects do you take an interest in?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, I haven't been in too many activities or projects. Most of them... The home things pretty well take up most of my time by the time supper and with the kids. I had joined one club, which it is a good club, it was MNL. But I quit because at night time I'd be so tired that I don't think I was much good.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Family decision making, who makes the decisions, you or your husband or both?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, the father is usually gone so mother gets stuck with it, right or wrong. And it's usually based on mutual agreement.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Some of those... No. Prior to your courtship, have you ever been married, divorced or widowed? You haven't, have you?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: No, no.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Then I wanted to know why. Your job career, that is... Well, I don't know. Who do you associate with? Your friends and neighbors around the community?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yes, just...

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Around here?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: We have some that are out of town. We have some real nice neighbors.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: I guess that answers most of the questions. Is there anything else that you can think of that you'd like to add about St. Mary's? You did say what was a thing that you like about St. Mary's. Is there anything you don't like about St. Mary's?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Well, I don't know. Well, St. Mary's still is working on their streets and stuff. I mean, our town can be improved. It has a lot of room for improvement as far as our streets, sidewalks, lighting, street lights at night. And as far as activities for the kids, now we don't have a show house, which would help. Or a bowling alley, roller skating rink. We don't have any of these type of things for our kids. And I think there'd be a lot less problems if we had something that the kids could do. Because now they bus them to Spokane to go roller skating. The different churches or groups, whatever, they take the kids and go to Spokane. And it would be nice if St. Mary's had some of this. So you wouldn't have to go to the expense of going that far. Ah!

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Is that... St. Mary's is really big enough to support something like that.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yes, it is. It's surprising how many kids we do have.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Are your children in flight?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: No, they're not. Jackie was going to join, but she got into Little League softball.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Oh, well that was an interesting thing to do.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: She and her in Little League softball. They're also kind of busy now for a couple months.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Are the girls in the boys' softball team?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: No, they're separate.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: They're separate from that team.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Yeah, the girls left theirs. Last year there was quite a squabble. The girls tried to get into the boys' Little League, which you probably read in the papers about it.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Yes, I did.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Of course, we had one daughter that did. They let them try out and everything, and then after they tried out, that's when they told them that girls couldn't join the boys, which kind of broke their hearts. Yes. Discrimination. The university kids did come up, girls and boys. I know, well, the county donated their dump trucks, and they took two and a half dump trucks' loads of debris off our place, and the boys helped clean out the pantry and the back porch, the garage, things that would have taken us weeks to do, they did in a few hours.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Was that Vista?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: I don't know what it was. They bused them up, there was two bus loads, and they'd come up, and they all worked very hard. They were all real nice kids. Some of the girls helped clean out, you know, scrubbing on some of the other people's houses. But they had a time limit, and when it hit four o'clock, they had to be at their bus.

speaker: Speaker 2
words: Oh, well, that was great, wasn't it?

speaker: Speaker 1
words: It was really a big boost. They really don't realize how much they did help.
